author: Arielle Breen
title: Chinook salmon responding to north winds, water temp changes - NewsBreak
text:
By Arielle Breen ,
6 hours ago The Aug. 26, 2026 weekly fishing report notes that anglers caught a few Chinook salmon from the Manistee North Pier, in the Manistee River channel and in Manistee Lake. (News Advocate/File Photo) The Department of Natural Resources’ weekly fishing report for Aug. 26 shows some of the most current conditions in the region and best methods.
Fishing tip This week’s report included a tips for salmon, walleye and perch in the fall and the DNR’s Michigan.gov/FishID website.
“Ask many anglers and they’ll tell you fall is a wonderful time to go fishing as fish prepare for the colder months by ramping up their feeding efforts,” the report says. “Most will target salmon, walleye, perch, panfish and bass and see much success when doing so.”
For salmon, many fish will return “very hungry to their natal streams throughout this month.”
The Fish ID website shows spots to locate them.
This season, large schools of walleye will move from the Great Lakes inland.
“By the end of September these fish will really be biting. Visit Michigan.gov/Walleye to learn more about techniques for targeting them,” the report states.
The report highlights Lake Michigan and Lake Erie as “great opportunities for perch fishing during the fall as the large schools head to shallow water.”
Local conditions Here’s what anglers said about recent fishing conditions in Manistee, Benzie and Mason counties.
Manistee
Manistee anglers targeting salmon found them both north and south of the port while trolling in depths from 70-300 feet of water.
“Fish were typically caught 60-80 feet down and at depths of 100-plus feet of water,” the report says. “Spoons, flies, and plugs worked best in the early mornings and late evenings.”
Early in the week, anglers caught a few Chinook salmon from the Manistee North Pier, in the Manistee River channel and in Manistee Lake.
“Anglers trolling in front of the pier heads also caught Chinook salmon on plugs and spoons,” reads part of the report.
Onekama
North winds “rolled the lake over,” bringing cooler water in.
Onekama anglers found good numbers of Chinook salmon fishing the Barrel lake formation and in front of Arcadia Bluffs Golf Club in the early mornings.
Most anglers had success with spoons and plugs.
Ludington
Ludington anglers caught Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and a few steelhead.
Success was reported by those who trolled straight out and south in 80-110 feet of water 35 feet down to the bottom.
Another good location was northwest up toward Big Sable Point in 60-120 feet of water while fishing 40 to 80-plus feet down or near the bottom.
“Plugs, spoons and flies worked best, the report states. “At the beginning of the week, Chinook salmon were caught while jigging or trolling in the harbor, in front of the piers and in Pere Marquette Lake.”
Frankfort
North winds rolled the lake over, bringing cooler water into Frankfort as well.
“Chinook salmon responded by moving into the harbor, directly out front, and into the river,” the report notes. “Breakwall anglers, jiggers and open-water trollers reported strong numbers. Coho salmon also moved into Platte Bay.”
